channel.title: Mister Translation
channel.description: A fresh translation of the Bible into modern English, made from the original Hebrew and Greek one chapter at a time.

item.title: 2 Peter 3
item.description: The mockers’ question, “Where is the promise of his presence?”; an earth formed out of water and through water, the world that perished in the flood, and the present heavens “stored up for fire”; “with the Lord one day is like a thousand years”; a Lord not slow but patient…

item.title: 2 Peter 2
item.description: The false teachers, closely parallel to Jude: “factions of destruction” and the Master who bought them denied; ⚠ angels cast into Tartarus and “chains of gloom,” Noah “the eighth,” Sodom and Gomorrah reduced to ashes and “righteous Lot”; glories blasphemed; spots and…

item.title: 1 Peter 5
item.description: To the elders from “a fellow elder”: “shepherd the flock of God,” not for shameful gain and not lording it over “the portions allotted to you,” and the chief shepherd’s unfading crown of glory; Proverbs 3:34 again, “God opposes the proud”; anxiety cast on God; the adversary…

item.title: 1 Peter 4
item.description: “Since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking”; the old life of revels and drinking parties, and neighbors “surprised” at the change; ⚠ the good news “proclaimed also to the dead,” with the readings and no verdict; “the end of all things…

item.title: 1 Peter 3
item.description: Wives and husbands: unbelieving husbands “won without a word,” “the hidden person of the heart,” Sarah who called Abraham “lord,” and “a weaker vessel” honored as a fellow heir of the grace of life. “Not repaying evil for evil”; Psalm 34; Isaiah 8 with Christ in the place of…

item.title: 1 Peter 2
item.description: “Like newborn infants, long for the unadulterated milk of the word.” Christ the living stone, “rejected by people but chosen and precious,” with Isaiah 28:16, Psalm 118:22 and Isaiah 8:14; “a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation,” word for word the Greek of Exodus…

item.title: James 5
item.description: “Come now, you rich”: wealth rotted, clothes moth-eaten, gold and silver rusted, and the rust a witness. The wages of the mowers, held back, “cry out,” and the cries have reached “the ears of Jehovah of armies.” “Be patient until the presence of the Lord,” like the farmer…

item.title: James 4
item.description: “Where do wars come from, and where do fights among you come from?” From “your pleasures that wage war in your members”; “you do not have, because you do not ask.” ⚠ “Adulteresses!” Friendship with the world is hostility toward God; “the spirit that he made to dwell in us…

item.title: James 3
item.description: “Let not many of you become teachers”: “we all trip in many ways.” A bit in a horse’s mouth, a very small steering oar, and “how small a fire sets how great a forest ablaze.” ⚠ The tongue “setting on fire the wheel of birth, and set on fire by Gehenna,” tamed by no one, “full…

item.title: James 2
item.description: “My brothers, you do not hold the faith … with acts of partiality, do you?” The man with gold rings and the poor man in filthy clothing walk into the synagogue, and one is told “sit there below my footstool.” “Did not God choose the poor?” The royal law, “love your neighbor…

item.title: Hebrews 13
item.description: The letter’s last chapter. “Let brotherly love abide”; “some have entertained angels without knowing it”; prisoners, marriage and money, and “I will never let go of you” with Psalm 118’s “Jehovah is my helper.” “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and forever.” ⚠…

item.title: Hebrews 12
item.description: “So great a cloud of witnesses”: run the race with endurance, looking to “the Author and Completer of faith.” ⚠ Proverbs 3 in the Greek, “he scourges every son whom he receives,” where the Hebrew has “as a father the son in whom he delights”; discipline as the mark of sons…

item.title: Hebrews 10
item.description: The law “a shadow of the good things to come”; “it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.” ⚠ Psalm 40 in the Greek, “a body you prepared for me,” where the Hebrew has “ears you have dug for me.” The priests stand; this one sat down, “one sacrifice…

item.title: Hebrews 9
item.description: The first tent and its furniture — lampstand, table, ⚠ a golden incense altar or censer, the ark with the jar of manna, Aaron’s rod and the tablets, and the cherubim over the place of atonement — and the high priest’s entry “once a year, not without blood.” Then Christ…

item.title: Hebrews 8
item.description: “The main point”: a high priest seated at the right hand of the Majesty, minister of “the true tent, which Jehovah pitched” — the words of the Greek of Numbers 24:6. The earthly priests serve “a copy and shadow,” made “according to the pattern” shown to Moses on the mountain.…

item.title: Hebrews 7
item.description: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, read from Genesis 14: “king of righteousness” and “king of peace,” ⚠ “without father, without mother, without genealogy” — the readings of that silence set side by side. Abraham’s tenth, and Levi who “paid tithes”…

item.title: Hebrews 6
item.description: “Let us be carried on to maturity”: the foundation of repentance, faith, washings and laying on of hands. Then ⚠ the hardest passage in the letter: for those who have “tasted the heavenly gift” and “fallen away,” it is “impossible to renew them again to repentance” — the…

item.title: Hebrews 5
item.description: Every high priest is “taken from among human beings,” able to “deal gently with the ignorant and those who go astray” because he is “surrounded by weakness,” and called by God like Aaron. So Christ was named by the one who said “You are my Son” and “a priest forever…

item.title: Hebrews 4
item.description: “Let us fear, then”: the rest the psalm closed is still open. God’s own rest on the seventh day, a “Today” spoken through David long afterward, and ⚠ “if Joshua had given them rest” — the Greek name is Iēsous, which the KJV prints “Jesus.” “A sabbath rest remains for the…

item.title: Hebrews 3
item.description: Jesus, “the apostle and high priest of our confession,” set beside Moses: Moses faithful in God’s house as an attendant, Christ as a Son over it, “and we are that house, if…” Then Psalm 95: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as at the Provocation, on the…

item.title: Hebrews 2
item.description: The letter’s first warning — “so that we do not drift away” — and then Psalm 8 read of Jesus: made “for a little while lower than the angels,” with the Hebrew’s elohim beside the Greek’s “angels,” and crowned after the suffering of death. ⚠ The printed Greek says he tasted…

item.title: Titus 3
item.description: The last chapter of the three Pastoral letters. Be subject to rulers and “obey” — the verb Peter used to refuse them at Acts 5:29 — and be gentle toward all people, “for we too were once senseless.” Then ⚠ “when the kindness and the love for humankind of God our Saviour…

item.title: Titus 2
item.description: What Titus is to teach on Crete, household by household: older men “temperate, dignified, sensible,” older women “teachers of what is good” who train the younger “to love their husbands, to love their children,” younger men, and Titus himself as the example; and one word…

item.title: 2 Timothy 4
item.description: The last chapter of the letter, and on the traditional reading the last words Paul wrote. ⚠ “Preach the word; stand ready in season and out of season,” for a time is coming when people will heap up teachers for themselves, “having itching ears,” and wander off to myths. Then…

item.title: 2 Timothy 3
item.description: ⚠ “In the last days difficult times will set in”: eighteen marks of the people in them, from “lovers of self” to “lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,” and “a form of godliness” with its power denied. Teachers who slip into households and take captive “silly women,”…

item.title: 2 Timothy 2
item.description: Paul, in chains, to his “child”: entrust the teaching to faithful people who will teach others, and suffer along with me — the soldier, the athlete crowned only if he competes “lawfully,” the farmer who labors. “Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead”; “the word of God…

item.title: 1 Timothy 6
item.description: ⚠ Slaves “under the yoke” and their masters — verses once quoted to defend slavery, set beside the same letter’s “slave-traders” and Paul’s “a beloved brother.” Then the teacher “sick” with word-quarrels who thinks “godliness is a means of gain,” “godliness with contentment…

item.title: 1 Timothy 5
item.description: The congregation as a family — older men as fathers, younger women as sisters — and the care of widows: “Honor widows who are truly widows,” children who “make a return to their forebears,” and the one who neglects his own “worse than an unbeliever.” ⚠ The list of widows…

item.title: 1 Timothy 4
item.description: ⚠ “In later times some will fall away from the faith”: liars “branded in their own conscience,” who forbid marriage and foods, answered with “everything created by God is good”; the verse’s later use against clerical celibacy is set beside the Catholic reply. Then “train…

item.title: 1 Timothy 3
item.description: The overseer and the servants. “Faithful is the saying”; the office of overseer and the list of what he must be, with ⚠ “the husband of one wife” and its four readings; a man who leads his own household, for “how will he take care of God’s congregation?” Then the servants…
